about:
Hudson Electric Sales Corp. has been based in Hawthorne, New York, since its establishment in 1972. The company operates as a privately held business, though specific ownership structure and founder names are not publicly documented.

The company functions as a supplier of industrial switchgear and power distribution equipment, offering electrical control systems and switchgear tailored for commercial, industrial, and institutional applications. Its product range includes industrial switchgear and power distribution equipment, supported by a staff of 50 to 99 employees who manage procurement, technical support, and logistics.

The firm serves customers across industrial, commercial, and institutional markets, providing equipment for power distribution and control systems in facilities such as manufacturing plants, office buildings, and public institutions. Its client base includes organizations that require reliable electrical infrastructure components.

The company has not publicly stated a specific founding mission or differentiator beyond its role as a supplier of electrical equipment.

name: Huetter Mill & Cabinet
old_description: We are a full service custom millwork and stair parts manufacturer for commercial, residential new construction, and remodeling projects including stair installations. Our manufacturing location makes custom cabinetry focusing primarily on commercial and large high-end projects but we also ship nationally.
about:
Huetter Mill & Cabinet operates from Murray, Utah, where it was founded in 1948 by Alfred Huetter, a German immigrant who began building window sash and custom millwork in a chicken coop behind his family home in the 1930s. The business remains family-owned, now led by President Gordon Huetter, Alfred’s son.

The company manufactures custom millwork, stair parts, handrails, and hardwood moldings from a dedicated production facility and showroom in Murray. It stocks moldings in alder, knotty alder, maple, poplar, cherry, and oak, maintains a library of custom knives for unique profiles, and produces curved stairways and complete stair systems. Inventory exceeds $1.2 million, and the firm uses advanced machinery staffed by skilled craftsmen to serve both commercial and high-end residential projects, shipping nationally.

Huetter Mill serves commercial construction, residential new builds, and remodeling markets, with a specialty in historic restoration. Past projects include the Utah Governor’s Mansion, Utah State Capitol, The Children’s Center, and O.C. Tanner renovations. Capabilities extend to schools, hospitals, tenant improvements, court buildings, and correctional facilities.

The company’s stated purpose is to provide a financially sound source for wholesale millwork and commercial shop products at reasonable cost, delivered efficiently by trained employees. Its motto, “Quality and Craftsmanship live in our Name,” reflects the multi-generational commitment to that standard.

name: Hunt & Noyer Furniture
old_description: Our small business was founded on tradition. We strongly believe in the importance of passing things down. Our namesake is an homage to Kyle's parents’ surnames, DesNoyer and Huntoon. Midwestern families made up of generations of hardworking craftsman that deserve our respect and admiration.
about:
Hunt & Noyer Furniture was established in 2013 in the Village of Clarkston, Michigan. The small business takes its name from the surnames of founder Kyle’s parents, DesNoyer and Huntoon, honoring a lineage of Midwestern craftsmen. Kyle launched the company to continue a family tradition of woodworking, building pieces that reflect a respect for heritage and a commitment to enduring quality.

The workshop produces a range of furniture including benches, dining tables, consoles, cabinets, and seating, with a focus on modern design executed through traditional handcrafting methods. They accept custom one-off commissions for private residences as well as larger-scale projects for public and corporate clients. Walnut is a signature material, selected and worked by hand for each piece.

The company serves residential customers, commercial and institutional clients, and interior designers through a trade program. Past projects include custom dining tables for homeowners in Michigan and Illinois, a solid walnut crib for a nursery in Jackson, MI, and consoles used as home-office workstations. Interior designers receive a trade discount on the existing collection.

Hunt & Noyer positions its work as heirloom-quality rather than trend-driven, emphasizing that “trends change, but quality is timeless.” The founder’s personal involvement in design and material selection, along with a philosophy rooted in American craftsmanship, is presented as the core differentiator.

name: ICON Injection Molding, Inc. Shipping / Receiving
old_description: ICON is an engineering-based company that takes a scientific approach to our design, qualification and manufacturing processes. We build customer confidence by showing you results.
about:
ICON Injection Molding, Inc. was founded in 2001 in Phoenix, Arizona, by three brothers—Danny, Philip, and Steve Kleitsch. The Kleitsches had worked in their father’s injection molding and tooling shop since the late 1970s, learning tool building and supplier relationships. After their father sold the business, the brothers launched their own family-owned company, naming it ICON after becoming the first custom molder in Arizona to run electric‑hybrid molding machines. Their motto, “Excellence from Art to Part,” was coined early by Danny Kleitsch and still guides the business.

The company provides custom plastic injection molding solutions, including tooling, machining, assembly, and secondary operations. Its facility houses 42 presses ranging from 15 to 720 tons, with capacity for further growth. Capabilities span automation, clean‑room molding, overmolding, rotary (vertical) molding, and custom packaging. A scientific molding approach uses statistical analysis to drive process stability, supported by a quality lab equipped with Keyence 3‑D inspection (to 0.00008 in tolerance), capability studies (CPK), Gage R&R, first‑article inspection, and IQ/OQ/PQ validation. ICON also offers global sourcing through domestic and offshore strategic partnerships, and a campus expansion dubbed “ICON 4” is underway.

ICON serves customers worldwide, from local Phoenix businesses to international clients, delivering both “Made in USA” parts and cost‑effective offshore options. The company works with original equipment manufacturers and supply‑chain partners across diverse sectors, though specific industries are not detailed in public materials.

The founders started ICON to apply a scientific, engineering‑based methodology to molding—preventing problems rather than detecting them. The family‑owned structure, with over 100 combined years of industry experience, underpins a culture of continual improvement and point‑of‑use quality.

name: IEG Plastics LLC
old_description: IEG Plastics was founded in 2004 and is headquartered in Bellefontaine, Ohio. We are a proud supplier of plastic parts and assemblies to the automotive and consumer goods industries.
about:
IEG Plastics LLC was founded in 2004 in Bellefontaine, Ohio. The company operates as a supplier of plastic parts and assemblies, serving primarily the automotive and consumer goods sectors. No founders are named in public materials, and ownership structure has not been disclosed.

The company provides plastic injection molding, mold building, and product design services under one roof. Its mold building capacity handles tools up to 20,000 pounds, and it offers both domestic and Asian mold sourcing with U.S.-based engineering changes and repair. Production capabilities include tight-tolerance molding to ±0.02 mm (±0.000787 in), insert molding, overmolding, robotic part handling, sonic welding, and assembly. An environmentally controlled metrology lab houses a Brown & Sharpe CMM, Micro-VU Vertex 311HC, Zeiss 3D light scanner, and other inspection equipment. Design work uses SolidWorks, Catia, and Pro/E, with DFM and Moldflow analysis available. The firm also runs prototypes and low-volume functional parts via 3D printing.

IEG Plastics serves the automotive, consumer goods, and sporting goods industries. Automotive work includes safety components that require adherence to strict quality standards such as APQP and PPAP. Consumer and sporting goods projects leverage the company’s experience with precision, high-volume parts.

The company emphasizes partnerships aimed at increasing productivity and reducing total cost. It cites in-house engineering and design, streamlined processes for short lead times, a quality management system certified to ISO 9001:2015, and the use of RJG process control and advanced scanning technology as differentiators. Operating on the Traction Entrepreneurial Operating System, IEG Plastics focuses on accountability and continuous improvement to deliver dock-to-stock quality on time.

about:
Founded in 1963, Industrial Electronic Supply (IES) has been headquartered in Baton Rouge, Louisiana for over six decades. The company does not disclose its ownership structure or the names of its founders.

IES operates as a distributor of industrial electronic components across five core categories: industrial controls, automation, drives, power distribution, and instrumentation. Its catalog features products from Siemens, Emerson, Turck, Banner Engineering, Rittal, Weidmüller, and Flowline, among others. Beyond product supply, IES provides technical services such as IO-Link integration support, condition monitoring for electrical control cabinets, predictive maintenance consulting, and 24/7 cloud-based monitoring. The company does not publish figures for facility size, employee count, or annual sales volume.

The company’s customer base spans aviation, logistics, maritime, brewing, power generation, oil and gas, chemical processing, water and wastewater, and general manufacturing. Concrete examples from its product announcements include cooling units for airport baggage-handling systems and port cranes, automation packages for a Texas brewery, pump control panels for irrigation and oilfield applications, and vibration sensors for predictive maintenance on production machinery.

IES highlights immediate availability of stocked valves and other components, along with specialized expertise in IO-Link communication and condition-monitoring platforms, as key differentiators. Its stated mission is to help industrial users reduce unplanned downtime and improve operational efficiency through data-driven insights and ready-to-ship inventory.

about:
ION Solar is headquartered in Ashland, Virginia, and operates as a residential solar installation company serving homeowners across the United States. The company does not disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founders in the provided materials.

The company provides a full-service solar installation process that begins with an on-site home assessment, followed by custom system design by an in-house engineering team, handling of permits and approvals, and final installation and activation. ION Solar manages financing, design, permitting, and installation, using Tier 1 solar panels, MLPE microinverters, and Tesla Powerwall 3 battery storage. To date, the company reports more than 85,000 completed installations nationwide.

ION Solar serves residential customers, with testimonials from homeowners in Virginia and other states highlighting reduced electricity bills and positive installation experiences. The company also references Solar Renewable Energy Certificates and roofing-related services, indicating a focus on residential renewable energy and home energy efficiency.

ION Solar differentiates itself through a “worry-free, done-for-you service” model that includes dedicated project coordinators, weekly check-ins, and a 10-year workmanship guarantee alongside 25-year product and 30-year power output warranties on panels. The company states its mission is to deliver a premium product and premium experience, backed by a satisfaction guarantee.

The company emphasizes its veteran‑owned status, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and a culture of continuous improvement and knowledge sharing as differentiators. It positions its expertise as U.S.-based and focused on tailoring solutions to each operation’s throughput and labor‑reduction goals.

about:
Founded in 2001, ICB Electronics, Inc. is based in Scottsboro, Alabama, where it operates a manufacturing facility on South Broad Street. The business serves manufacturers throughout the South and is led by Jack O’Rear as the primary point of contact.

ICB Electronics produces cable and wire harness assemblies with a focus on high-mix, low-volume orders. Processes cover wire stripping, cutting, marking, hand soldering, and small box builds. The shop runs a KOMAX Gamma 333pc and a Cosmic 60R automatic wire processing machines, supported by a range of die sets. The quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015 for the manufacturing and testing of cable and harness assemblies.

The product range includes power distribution cables, coaxial cables, communication cables, industrial cables, ribbon cables, and individual cable assemblies. Customers are primarily manufacturers in the southeastern United States who need flexible, high-mix harness production.

The company describes its mission as changing the future of harness manufacturing through creative manufacturing solutions. It emphasizes that a truly flexible vendor ensures usability, longevity, and vibrant product response in changing markets.

name: Idaho Milk Products
old_description: Our brand new ice cream facility is open! We are excited to bring this business to our home right here in the Magic Valley. Our mission remains the same, we are daring food to be better. Come and see how we are innovating the ice cream industry.
about:
Idaho Milk Products operates from Jerome, Idaho, in the Magic Valley region. The company recently opened a new ice cream and blending facility, expanding its integrated dairy ingredient production. Ownership details and founding year are not publicly disclosed.

The company produces dairy ingredients including milk protein, milk permeate, and cream, and manufactures ice cream and custom blends at a facility rated for 16,000 lbs/hr. Flexible batch sizes are accommodated, and post-mixing sifting is performed on a Russel Finnex Compact 1200 to ensure product purity. An on-site Milk Innovation Center staffed by food scientists collaborates directly with customer R&D teams to develop market-ready formulations. The integrated operation spans from farm sourcing through final bagging, emphasizing freshness, consistency, and traceability.

Primary customers are dairy and food-and-beverage manufacturers seeking high-protein ingredients, custom blending, and ice cream production. The company also lists energy and industry sectors among its served markets. Concrete examples include partnerships for high-protein product development and formulation support using milk permeate powder.

Idaho Milk Products states its mission is to dare food to be better, differentiating itself through an integrated farm-to-bag supply chain, direct R&D collaboration via its Milk Innovation Center, sustainable stewardship commitments, and a focus on responsible community impact.
